claims.claim: EQT Corporation identity and NYSE:EQT tradability are validated in the current packet; current scoring lineage uses issuer/SEC primary filings and keeps the independent current market-cap observation separate from issuer-origin claims.
Duplicate-origin collapse is preserved: repeated uses of the Q2 earnings release and Q2 10-Q resolve to two primary origin fingerprints rather than being counted as independent corroboration.

risks.risk: Issuer releases are primary evidence but not independent corroboration of issuer claims; commodity-price and basis sensitivity remain material.

unknowns.unknown: No independent source in this run corroborates every operating claim; confidence is reduced accordingly rather than treating issuer repetition as independence.

claims.claim: Operating momentum is strong: Q1 2026 sales volume exceeded guidance, capex was below the low end, operating costs were below guidance, quarterly free cash flow reached $1.832B, and net debt fell to $5.666B from $7.690B at year-end 2025; Q2 cumulative evidence continued above-guidance production and below-guidance capex.

Balance-sheet risk is improving but remains material: total debt fell to about $6.0B at Q1 2026 and EQT executed a 2026 debt tender; commodity prices, basis differentials and infrastructure constraints remain major external drivers.
Vertical integration and more than 2,000 miles of pipeline infrastructure broaden capability and lower modeled corporate breakeven, but do not eliminate commodity or transport risk.

risks.risk: Natural-gas commodity prices and Appalachian basis/transport constraints can overwhelm operating gains.
Long-duration LNG logistics commitments beginning in 2028 add utilization and execution exposure before realized economics are observable.
Current market capitalization near $31.3B leaves valuation dependent on durable free-cash-flow delivery and commodity assumptions.

unknowns.unknown: Realized economics of future LNG vessel capacity and downside utilization cases remain unproven.
Current evidence does not establish exceptional supplier redundancy across all critical operating inputs.

thesisQuality.basis: Strong recurring demand for low-cost natural gas, integrated upstream/midstream assets and demonstrated operating execution support the strong band; commodity dependence prevents exceptional treatment.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q1 2026 record $1.832B free cash flow, above-guidance production, below-guidance capex/costs and net-debt reduction to $5.666B, followed by Q2 above-guidance production and below-guidance capex, support the upper strong band.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September 2026 market capitalization around $31.27B against strong cash generation offers plausible upside but remains highly sensitive to gas prices and does not establish compelling cross-cycle asymmetry.

catalystScore.basis: Debt reduction, domestic power-demand growth and LNG market-access development are identifiable catalysts, though LNG realization extends into 2028 and remains uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Proxy disclosure and demonstrated capital allocation toward deleveraging support a strong but not exceptional governance assessment.

alignment2036.basis: Large-scale gas supply and integrated transport infrastructure serve durable power, heating, industrial and LNG needs, with growing power demand cited by the company; transition and commodity uncertainty cap the score below exceptional.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Integrated upstream, midstream and marketing capabilities plus domestic power and LNG channels provide several demand paths using the same gas resource base.

bottleneckControl.basis: Ownership of more than 2,000 miles of pipeline infrastructure and integrated Appalachian operations provides meaningful control of transport capacity, but external basis and infrastructure constraints remain.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Low-cost integrated operations, domestic power exposure and LNG optionality improve resilience across demand scenarios, while commodity and basis sensitivity remain material.

substitutionResilience.basis: Integrated low-cost gas economics and infrastructure create replacement friction, but alternative fuels, renewables/storage and competing basins remain credible substitutes over time.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Integrated upstream/midstream operations and demonstrated severe-weather execution provide resilience evidence; complete redundancy across critical suppliers is not established.

pricingPower.basis: Marketing optimization, integrated transport and tighter realized differentials show some economic capture, but gas remains commodity-priced and exposed to basis swings.

riskEvidence.basis: Commodity-price, basis/transport and future LNG utilization risks are material, partly offset by low-cost integrated operations and rapid deleveraging.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Identity/tradability are validated and multiple current primary filings cover operations, balance sheet, governance and strategy; confidence is reduced because most operating facts are issuer-origin and independent current evidence is primarily valuation data.

scoreRecord.thesis: EQT combines low-cost Appalachian gas production with integrated midstream and marketing infrastructure, improving cash generation, market access and resilience while retaining material commodity-cycle exposure.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Commodity and basis volatility, transport constraints and uncertain economics of future LNG commitments can overwhelm company-level execution gains.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Continued 2026 deleveraging and free-cash-flow delivery, followed by evidence that domestic power/LNG market-access initiatives convert into durable realized economics.

scoreBreakdown.note: Methodology 1.0 weighted component score less risk*0.16; confidence 86 exceeds publication floor, so no additional unsupported confidence uplift is applied.
